byTheNumbers.title: The year in numbers
byTheNumbers.standfirst: 309 million people, nearly 72 in 100 online and more mobile subscriptions than people, a baby born in 2010 could expect to live to 78.

items.title: Population
items.summary: The 2010 census counted 308.7 million people, 87.4 to the square mile.

sources.label: U.S. Census Bureau: Decennial census historical facts, 2010
World Bank, World Development Indicators: Population, total

items.title: Life expectancy at birth
items.summary: A baby born in 2010 could expect to live about 78.5 years.

items.title: Online
items.summary: About 72 percent of Americans used the internet in 2010.

sources.label: World Bank, World Development Indicators: Individuals using the Internet (% of population)

items.title: Mobile phones
items.summary: There were about 92 mobile subscriptions for every 100 people.

items.title: Infant deaths
items.summary: About 6 of every 1,000 babies died before their first birthday.

items.title: Jobs
items.summary: In February 2010 payroll employment hit a post-recession low of 129,655,000.

byTheNumbers.scarcityNote: Literacy, household size, vehicle counts and wages were not found for 2010 from a source we opened.

foodAndKitchen.title: Food and the kitchen

items.title: A tomato shortage
items.summary: A U.S. tomato shortage began in March 2010 and lasted until April.

foodAndKitchen.scarcityNote: We could not find sourced 2010 food prices or meals beyond a tomato shortage.

clothingAndStyle.title: What people wore
clothingAndStyle.standfirst: Skinny jeans and hoodies, slim suits and plaid shirts, with fast fashion supplying vintage-inspired styles.

items.title: Skinny jeans
items.summary: Low-rise skinny jeans, often in acid wash or bright denim, stayed a dominant women's silhouette in the early 2010s, and men's skinny jeans rose in popularity.

items.title: Hoodies
items.summary: Slim-fitting men's hoodies, often V-necked, and women's zip-up hoodies were popular, and American teens wore logo hoodies from Abercrombie & Fitch, Hollister and Aéropostale.

items.title: Plaid shirts and cutoffs
items.summary: Teens in 2010 wore plaid shirts, cutoff shorts and studded accessories.

items.title: The Mad Men suit
items.summary: Mad Men-inspired slim grey two-piece suits made a comeback in the workplace in the early 2010s.

items.title: Vintage by the rack
items.summary: Fast-fashion retailers such as Topshop, Forever 21 and H&M popularised vintage-inspired styles in the early 2010s.

items.title: Indie and hipster
items.summary: By the early 2010s indie clothing in the United States and elsewhere had moved to a more grown-up look in earth tones, with leggings and beanies; Ugg boots were among the early-to-mid 2010s accessories.

workAndWages.title: Work and wages
workAndWages.scarcityNote: We could not find sourced 2010 wage, hours or minimum-wage figures; the jobs count is under The year in numbers.

schoolAndChildhood.title: Growing up
schoolAndChildhood.scarcityNote: We could not find sourced 2010 school-year or enrolment figures.

gettingAround.title: Getting around
gettingAround.standfirst: Several states banned texting at the wheel, and a carmaker fixed its accelerators.

items.title: No texting at the wheel
items.summary: Illinois' texting-while-driving ban took effect on 1 January 2010 and bans began on 1 July in several states, including Iowa and Wyoming.

items.title: The Toyota recall
items.summary: On 1 February 2010 Toyota announced a fix for accelerator problems and recalled cars in the United States.

gettingAround.scarcityNote: We could not find sourced 2010 fares, journey times or vehicle counts.

keepingInTouch.title: Keeping in touch
keepingInTouch.scarcityNote: We could not find sourced 2010 postage, text-message or call-rate figures; the new devices and apps are in the spotlight.

healthAndMedicine.title: Health and medicine
healthAndMedicine.standfirst: A health-care law was signed, and North Carolina banned smoking in bars and restaurants.

items.title: The Affordable Care Act
items.summary: President Obama signed the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act on 23 March 2010; from 23 September 2010 young adults could stay on a parent's plan until age 26.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act

items.title: Smoke-free bars
items.summary: North Carolina banned smoking in bars, restaurants and other public places on 2 January 2010, with exemptions for cigar bars, private clubs and some hotels.

healthAndMedicine.scarcityNote: We could not find sourced 2010 doctor fees, hospital costs or vaccination figures.

leisureAndFun.title: Evenings, weekends and festivals
leisureAndFun.standfirst: A war film swept the Oscars, an animated sequel became Pixar's biggest hit, and the Saints won the Super Bowl.

items.title: The Hurt Locker
items.summary: The Hurt Locker won six Academy Awards, including Best Picture and Best Director, on 7 March 2010.

items.title: At the cinema
items.summary: How to Train Your Dragon opened on 26 March, Iron Man 2 on 7 May and Toy Story 3 on 18 June 2010, becoming Pixar's biggest financial success to that point.

items.title: Adventure Time
items.summary: Adventure Time premiered on Cartoon Network on 5 April 2010.

items.title: Super Bowl XLIV
items.summary: The New Orleans Saints beat the Indianapolis Colts 31-17 in Super Bowl XLIV on 7 February 2010.

items.title: Vancouver Winter Olympics
items.summary: The Winter Olympics were held in Vancouver from 12 to 28 February 2010.

spotlight.title: Smartphones and apps
spotlight.standfirst: A tablet and a photo-sharing app arrived in 2010, in a year when there were more mobile subscriptions than people.

items.title: The iPad
items.summary: Apple's first iPad, announced on 27 January 2010, went on sale on 3 April for $499 with a 9.7-inch touchscreen; 300,000 were sold on the first day.
items.metric: Price of the first iPad (Wi-Fi, base model)

items.title: A million in a month
items.summary: Apple had sold a million iPads by 3 May 2010 and 3 million after 80 days.

items.title: Instagram
items.summary: Kevin Systrom and Mike Krieger launched Instagram for iOS on 6 October 2010, after refocusing a check-in app called Burbn on photo sharing.

items.title: A million in two months
items.summary: Instagram reached 1 million registered users in two months and 10 million in a year; its first post, from South Beach Harbor, was on 16 July 2010.

items.title: Google and the cyber attack
items.summary: On 13 January 2010 Google said it had been the target of a cyber attack from China, which led it to consider leaving China.
